gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-orbit: Red Hat Display draws every stroke like a marker, with daylight showing inside each curve. And Orbit, in sans-serif form, lets its curves stop short and keeps each character floating apart from the next.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-gentium-plus: Gentium Plus opens each c like the mouth of a pitcher. Oswald packs its rows tight and strong above it, and that tension is the whole appeal.
gen-almendra-display-gf-anuphan: Ornate and bookish, Almendra Display keeps its letters from pinching shut while its x-height stands tall. Anuphan's big round bowls and open curves sit beneath.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-science-gothic: Science Gothic sets its stroke ends far apart, so you seem to take in one letter at a time. Red Hat Display adds a marker-like line above.
gen-orbitron-noto-serif: Precise, minimal Orbitron spreads its letters wide, every bar the same thickness along the line. Noto Serif is the opposite, with a light swell in each bowl like pressed glass and a prominent x-height.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-gowun-batang: Oswald knits its rows of text tight and strong. Gowun Batang cuts its terminals back to leave a big gap, so a long passage feels refined and literary.
gen-almendra-display-gf-arimo: Arimo reads tall and neutral, with spacious gaps in its rounded glyphs. Over a long stretch it stays professional and easy on the eye, while Almendra Display handles the ornate, literary flourish.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-syncopate: Syncopate draws its open letters with a technical-pen steadiness and spaces them like rungs on a rope ladder. And Red Hat Display adds a bold, marker-like line with daylight in every curve.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-habibi: Habibi reads traditional and editorial, with a clear channel leading into each round letter. And Oswald does what it does best, packing confident, strong rows of text tightly together.
